newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: INTERVIEW-Shell Philippines sees local price wars.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Shell Philippines sees local price wars.

text.p: The deregulation of the Philippines oil industry later this week is expected to usher in local price wars and heightened competition, a top official of Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp (PSPC) said.

"We will see price wars, maybe not immediately, but over time, when new players come in. I expect local price wars although not throughout the country as that hardly happens. I also expect more competition for customers in the consumer market," Reinier Willems, chief executive officer of PSPC, told Reuters in an interview on Monday.

PSPC, a member of the Royal Dutch/Shell group of companies, is one of the country's three oil refiners. The others include Petron Corp and Caltex Philippines Inc, a unit of Caltex (Petroleum) Inc which is a joint venture of Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc.

Willems added there will likely be no drastic changes in local pump prices with the start of full deregulation on February 8 despite fears expressed by citizens groups that prices will sharply increase once there is no government control.

He said product prices should rise by an average of between 10 and 14 centavos (0.38 to 0.53 U.S. cents) per litre immediately after deregulation. Regular gasoline currently sells at 10.20 pesos per litre while diesel sells at 8.43 pesos per litre.
Once deregulation is in force, oil refiners will no longer be tied down to an eight percent return-on-rate base or to any oil pricing formula.
The Department of Energy said in a statement that refiners can set domestic petroleum prices based either on Singapore Posted Prices (SPP) or on crude prices once the industry is fully deregulated.
Willems said Singapore Posted Prices will be a good benchmark as Shell computes oil-based product prices for the domestic market.

He said the company will likely maintain the use of the automatic oil pricing formula which the energy department adopted when it started the partial deregulation of the oil industry in August last year.

The formula allowed monthly adjustments on or before the third Monday of every month using movements in Singapore Posted Prices as a benchmark instead of the previous bi-monthly adjustments pegged on crude prices.

"What we want to show to the people is that even with freer prices, there won't be any dramatic change. The formula will be the most practical way for the next couple of months to get ourselves into the mode of free pricing rather than daily changing prices, unless, of course, something dramatic happens in the world market," said Willems.

A source from Caltex (Philippines) Inc said the company is also planning to continue with using the automatic oil price mechanism for a few more months. Petron officials were not immediately available for comment.
Willems said that aside from competing in terms of pricing, full deregulation will see players contending among themselves in terms of quality of products and service.

"Prices will vary per station throughout the country. Some of us may price higher but give excellent service while others may say we don't care about service but just offer the cheapest product," said Willems.
"We will try to be the best supplier, the customer's first choice in terms of quality, service and pricing," he added. ($1 = 26.30 pesos)
